description: Random sampler: a jittery internal clock split into two streams of random gates, and three random voltages shaped by a distribution, a quantiser and a loopable memory

params.text: Switches the deja vu loop on for the gate section, so its random decisions are recycled instead of freshly drawn
Switches the deja vu loop on for the voltage section, so its random values are recycled instead of freshly drawn
Counter-clockwise of noon it sets how likely past random values are to be reused, reaching a locked loop at noon; clockwise of noon it sets how likely the loop is to jump to a random place in itself
Sets the rate of the master clock, 120 BPM at noon; with a clock patched into the t section it divides or multiplies that clock instead
Sets the width and shape of the distribution the voltages are drawn from: a fixed voltage counter-clockwise, a bell curve at noon, an even spread past that, and only the two extremes fully clockwise
Cycles how the master clock is split between the two gate outputs: a coin toss at each pulse, random multiplication and division, or an alternation like a kick and snare pattern
Cycles how the three voltage outputs answer the spread, bias and steps settings: all three alike, the outer two opposed to the middle one, or a tilt graded across them
Sets the length of the deja vu loop, from one step to sixteen
Sets how likely a gate is to land on the first gate output rather than the third
Skews the random voltages towards the bottom or the top of the range without moving the range itself
Cycles the clock range, leaving the rate as the knob sets it or dividing or multiplying it by four
Cycles the range of the random voltage outputs between 0-2V, 0-5V and -5V to 5V
Switches on external processing, where the voltage section samples whatever is patched into the X spread input instead of drawing its own random numbers
Sets how far the clock wanders from steady time, from exact through the drift of a human player to complete chaos
Counter-clockwise of noon it smooths the random voltages into slopes and curves; clockwise of noon it quantises them to a scale and then strips notes out of that scale until only the root is left

inputs.text: Adds to the gate bias knob, 5V covering the whole knob range
Adds to the voltage bias knob, 5V covering the whole knob range
An external clock for the gate section, read high at 1.7V, taking the place of the internal one; the RATE knob then divides or multiplies it
Modulates the clock rate, each volt doubling or halving it
Adds to the JITTER knob, 5V covering the whole knob range
Adds to the DEJA VU knob, 5V covering the whole knob range
Adds to the STEPS knob, 5V covering the whole knob range
Adds to the SPREAD knob, 5V covering the whole knob range; in external processing mode the voltage here is sampled in place of the internal random source
Clocks all three random voltage outputs together, read high at 1.7V, in place of the gates from the t section

outputs.text: A 10V gate whenever the master clock's pulse is sent to this output by the t section
The master clock itself, a 10V gate with an even duty cycle
A random voltage stepped at a division of the clock chosen in the menu, anywhere from a sixty-fourth of that clock to the clock itself
A random voltage drawn at each clock pulse from the distribution set by SPREAD and BIAS and shaped by STEPS

notes: the module is monophonic: every output carries one channel.
menu: T mode — sets how the clock is split between the gate outputs: Complementary Bernoulli, Clusters, Drums, Independent Bernoulli, Divider, Three states or Markov
T range — sets the clock range to 1/4x, 1x or 4x, the same choice the clock range button steps through
X mode — sets how the three voltage outputs answer the knobs: Identical, Bump or Tilt, the same choice the X mode button steps through
X range — sets the range of the random voltage outputs to Narrow, Positive or Full, the same choice the output voltage range button steps through
Scales — picks the scale the STEPS knob quantises to: Major, Minor, Pentatonic, Pelog, Raag Bhairav That or Raag Shri
Internal X clock source — picks which of the three t streams clocks the three X outputs when nothing is patched into the X clock input, either one stream each or one stream driving all three
Y divider ratio — sets how far the Y output is divided down, from 1/64 through 1/48, 1/32, 1/24, 1/16, 1/12, 1/8, 1/6, 1/4, 1/3 and 1/2 to 1
